sentences.text:
The brief facts of the case are that on 22.10.2007, the deceased Raja Khan and Narayan Patel,
along with injured Rinku alias Kashiram, were travelling on a motorcycle and proceeding towards their house.

When they reached in front of Krishna Tent House near Banda barrier, the offending truck, driven in rash and negligent manner by the driver/owner, dashed against the motorcycle,
resulting in death of Raja Khan and Narayan Patel as also causing injuries to Rinku @ Kashiram.

4. For the death of Raja Khan and Narayan Patel and for the injuries sustained by Rinku, the claimants filed claim petitions before the Claims Tribunal under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation.

The appellant-Insurance Company filed its reply denying the averments of the claim petitions on the ground that, at the time of accident, the driver was not holding a valid and effective driving license and permit, and that the vehicle was being driven in violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
5. The Tribunal, after framing the issues, recorded the evidence.
Non- applicant No.1, owner/driver Kailash, examined himself and adduced evidence.

Upon considering the evidence adduced by the claimants and by NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:37067 3 MA-4189-2008 the owner/driver, the Tribunal recorded its finding in paragraph 12 of the award, holding that no credible or positive evidence had been adduced by the Insurance Company on the issue of breach of policy conditions relating to driving license and permit.
On the other hand, the Tribunal found that the offending vehicle was being driven under a valid and effective license.
Accordingly, it was held that violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy was not proved.

6. The present two appeals and civil revision have been filed by the appellant- Insurance Company mainly on the ground that the finding recorded by the Tribunal in paragraph 12 of the award,
relating to breach of policy conditions, is illegal and perverse.

It is argued that the driver/owner Kailash himself appeared in the witness box and, in paragraph 10 of his cross-examination,
admitted the particulars of his driving license, permit, and insurance policy.

These documents were duly exhibited and proved as Ex.D1, Ex. D2, Ex. D3, Ex. D4 and Ex. D5.
7. Ex. D2 is the permit issued for the period 24.10.2007 to 23.02.2008, whereas Ex. D4 contains particulars of the driving license valid from 05.06.2002 to 04.06.2005.
Thus, on the date of accident i.e. 22.10.2007, the driver/owner of the insured truck did not possess a valid driving license or permit.

This clearly constituted a violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy (Ex.
D5).
Since the driver/owner himself admitted the aforesaid documents in cross-examination, the appellant-Insurance Company was not required to adduce further evidence with respect to the admitted facts.

Accordingly, the finding recorded by the learned Tribunal on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:37067 4 MA-4189-2008 the issue of breach of policy conditions is contrary to the documentary evidence, perverse, and cannot be sustained.
It is therefore set aside.

8. Clearly, the offending vehicle, bearing registration No. M.P.-15 P/9566, was being driven by the owner/driver without a valid permit and license, and thus in violation of the terms and conditions of the policy.
Consequently, the appellant-Insurance Company is exonerated from liability to pay compensation.
Respondent Kailash, owner/driver of the vehicle, is held liable to pay compensation to the claimants.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Respondent Kailash, owner/driver of the vehicle, is held liable to pay compensation to the claimants.
